results.title: Price Discrimination in the Online Airline Market: An Empirical Study
results.content: Over the course of six weeks, we acquire each day at four different time stamps pricing data of three different airlines (i.e., Alitalia, Ryanair, and Lufthansa) for one national and for one continental itinerary to determine whether price discrimination occurs. The flight data obtained from the websites are also compared to a control group in order establish if the observed airlines use price discrimination when they have access to customers’ information. The goal of this research is to examine whether some airlines apply price discrimination based on the individual data that they collect from the customers through their direct booking channels, i.e., their websites. In order to determine whether the observed airlines make use of price discrimination, the flight data that is collected from their websites have to be compared with a control group. Over the course of six weeks, we acquired each day at four different time stamps pricing data of three different airlines (i.e., Alitalia, Ryanair, and Lufthansa) for one Italian and for one European itinerary to determine whether price discrimination occurs.
